clues: This city sits in an arc of land at the far top end of a long fjord. Green hills and mountains surround it on every other side.
Because this city sits so far north, summer days stretch past 18 hours and it never gets fully dark at night. In midwinter, daylight shrinks to about 6 hours.
King Haakon V was the first king to live in this city for good, around the year 1300. It has been counted as the land's capital ever since his reign.
Each year, this town hands out the Nobel Peace Prize. Folk all through the world know that prize as a great prize for peace.
Norway is run from this town, and its work of state is done here. More folk live in its streets than in any town in the land.
